sentences.text: This present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 01.07.2008, passed in MVC No.390/2007 by XVth Additional MACT, Jabalpur.
By the said award, learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and granted compensation to the tune of Rs.21,909/-- along with the interest of 6% per annum.

2. Factual matrix of the case is that on 21.10.2005 at about 7:00 P.M. claimant Ruplal aged about 21 years met with an accident, as a result he sustained grievous injuries on his head and other parts of the body.
Therefore, claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act before the Tribunal claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.8,70,000/-.
Learned Claims Tribunal found that the accident was caused by respondent no.1 due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56307 2 MA-4254-2009 Company on the unfortunate day.
On account of accident, the appellant/claimant sustained grievous injuries and remained hospitalized for a period of 5 days.

The learned Tribunal after appreciating the evidence on record, partly allowed the claim petition and awarded an amount of Rs.14,909/- for medical expenses, Rs.3,000/- for special diet,
Rs.1,000/- for loss of income during treatment and Rs.3,000/- for pain and suffering.
Thus, in all a sum of Rs.21,909/- has been awarded as against the claim of Rs.8,70,000/-.
3. It is not in dispute that respondent no.1 was responsible for causing the accident and the offending vehicle was insured with respondent no.3 on the date of accident.
The Tribunal has exonerated the insurance company because as per the policy, the owner of the offending vehicle did not pay the premium of pillion rider of the vehicle.
The next question for determination in this appeal is whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?.

4. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

5. After going through the record and hearing the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, I find that Tribunal has awarded lower side amount under the heads of special diet, loss of income, pain and suffering, attender and transportation.
6. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation by a sum of Rs.20,000/- in lump sum.
The enhanced amount of Rs.20,000/- shall also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56307 3 MA-4254-2009 carry the same interest as has been awarded by the Tribunal.

7. Therefore, in view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants interference to enhance the compensation by a lump sum amount of Rs.20,000/-.
Appellant is not entitled for any interest for the delayed period.
8. So far as the liability to pay compensation is concerned, as per the policy Ex.D/1, it is clear that it is a package policy, so the pillion rider is also covered under it.
Therefore, the finding of exoneration of insurance company is reversed and the Insurance Company is held liable to pay the compensation amount to the claimant.

It is also worthy to note that the High Court, after referring to individual circulars issued by various insurance companies, eventually stated thus:-
"In view of the aforesaid, it is clear that the comprehensive/package policy of a two wheeler covers a pillion rider and comprehensive/package policy of a private car c o v e r s t h e o c c u p a n t s a n d w h e r e t h e v e h i c l e i s c o v e r e d u n d e r a comprehensive/package policy, there is no need for Motor Accident Claims Tribunal to go into the question whether the Insurance Company is liable to compensate for the death or injury of a pillion rider on a two-wheeler or the occupants in a private car.
In fact, in view of the TAC's directives and those of the IRDA, such a plea was not permissible and ought not to have been raised as, for instance, it was done in the present case."

26. In view of the aforesaid factual position, there is no scintilla of doubt that a " c o m p r e h e n s i v e / p a c k a g e p o l i c y " w o u l d c o v e r t h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

There is no cavil that an "Act Policy" stands on a different footing from a "Comprehensive/Package Policy".

As the circulars have made the position very clear and the IRDA,
which is presently the statutory authority, has commanded the insurance companies stating that a "Comprehensive/Package Policy" covers the liability, there cannot be any dispute in that regard.

We may hasten to clarify that the earlier pronouncements were rendered in respect of the "Act Policy"
which admittedly cannot cover a third party risk of an occupant in a car.
But, if the policy is a "Comprehensive/Package Policy", the liability would be covered.

We are disposed to think that there is no necessity to refer the present matter to a larger Bench as the IRDA,
which is presently the statutory authority, has clarified the position by issuing circulars which have been reproduced in the judgment by the Delhi High Court and we have also reproduced the same."

In view of the foregoing discussion, appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
i.
The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against them.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
